novel_features.name: Meeting prep pack
novel_features.description: One command before a call: the meeting's attendees, their company, open deals, and transcript excerpts from past meetings with that company.
novel_features.rationale: Assembled from the local mirror with transcript full-text search; Clarify's hosted MCP needs four to six online calls for the same picture.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when the task is preparing for one specific upcoming meeting rather than fetching raw records. Requires a synced local mirror (sync --resources resources --path-context object=<type> first).
novel_features.group: Rituals the CRM knows but cannot run

novel_features.name: Morning briefing
novel_features.description: Start-of-day overview: today's meetings joined to their companies, open deals, and yesterday's record activity, on one screen.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-entity join across meetings, companies, deals, and activities in local SQLite; the API has no analytics or briefing endpoint.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for a whole-day overview; use prep for a single meeting. Requires a synced local mirror (sync --resources resources --path-context object=<type> first).
novel_features.group: Rituals the CRM knows but cannot run

novel_features.name: Follow-up gaps
novel_features.description: The dropped-ball list: meetings with no subsequent activity, comment, or task on the linked deal or company.
novel_features.rationale: A local anti-join the upstream API cannot express (no OR across fields, no gap queries).
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run it after a busy week to find meetings that never got a follow-up; --no-deal also surfaces companies with meetings but no open deal. Requires a synced local mirror (sync --resources resources --path-context object=<type> first).
novel_features.group: Rituals the CRM knows but cannot run

novel_features.name: Stale-deal report
novel_features.description: Open deals with no activity in N days, grouped by pipeline stage.
novel_features.rationale: Aggregates over record update timestamps in the local mirror; Clarify's API ships no analytics endpoints.
novel_features.why_it_matters: The Monday pipeline-review question answered in one command instead of a CSV export. Requires a synced local mirror (sync --resources resources --path-context object=<type> first).
novel_features.group: Pipeline analytics the API does not have

novel_features.name: Record dossier
novel_features.description: A complete background bundle on any record: fields, relationships, activities, comments, and related meetings with transcript references, in one compact payload.
novel_features.rationale: Replaces the hosted MCP's multi-call chain with a single local-first command shaped for agent context windows.
novel_features.why_it_matters: The one-call answer to 'tell me everything about this person/company/deal' — use prep instead when the subject is a specific upcoming meeting. Requires a synced local mirror.

novel_features.name: Pipeline velocity
novel_features.description: Per-stage dwell time and stage-to-stage conversion counts, accrued from a local stage-history table across repeated runs (the first run reports the current stage distribution).
novel_features.rationale: Computed from a stage-snapshot table maintained at sync time — history no Clarify surface keeps.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers 'how long do deals sit in each stage' without exporting anything to a spreadsheet. Requires a synced local mirror; dwell and conversion analytics build up as you re-run sync and velocity over time.
novel_features.group: Pipeline analytics the API does not have

novel_features.name: Duplicate finder
novel_features.description: Finds likely duplicate people or companies by shared email, domain, or normalized name, and prints ready-to-run merge commands.
novel_features.rationale: Local GROUP BY over the mirror paired with Clarify's record-merges endpoint; the auto-capture engine makes dupes inevitable.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Weekly hygiene sweep for auto-built CRM data; each finding comes with the exact merge invocation to fix it. Requires a synced local mirror (sync --resources resources --path-context object=<type> first).
novel_features.group: Pipeline analytics the API does not have

narrative.headline: Every Clarify API operation as a typed command, plus the morning briefing, meeting prep, and pipeline analytics the autonomous CRM knows about but cannot run.
narrative.value_prop: Clarify auto-builds your CRM from email, calendar, and meetings, but its only programmatic surfaces are a hosted MCP server and raw curl. This CLI covers all 75 API operations with the api-key auth scheme and JSON:API envelope handled natively, keeps a local SQLite mirror with transcript full-text search, and adds commands like prep, brief, followup, and dossier that no Clarify surface offers.
narrative.auth_narrative: Clarify authenticates with an API key sent as `Authorization: api-key <key>` — not a Bearer token. Create a Personal key in Clarify under Settings, API Keys, then set `CLARIFY_API_KEY` to the raw key; the CLI adds the `api-key` scheme prefix for you. Every request is scoped to a workspace slug (visible in your Clarify login URL); set it once with `CLARIFY_WORKSPACE` or the config file.

quickstart.comment: verify the binary, config, and auth wiring before touching the API
mirror one object type locally; repeat with object=person, company, meeting, task to mirror them all
start-of-day overview: today's meetings, their companies, and open deals
deals going cold, grouped by stage
full-text search across everything synced, including meeting transcripts

troubleshoots.symptom: 401 Invalid API key even though the key is correct
troubleshoots.fix: Clarify keys are workspace-scoped: confirm CLARIFY_WORKSPACE matches the workspace the key was created in, and that the key is a Personal key from Settings, API Keys.

troubleshoots.symptom: Multi-value fields like email_addresses fail to write
troubleshoots.fix: Collection fields take {"items": [...]} — pass --email-addresses as a JSON object with an items array, not a bare list.
Use the bulk endpoints (records bulk) instead of per-record calls; the limit is 3000 requests per minute per endpoint and the client honors Retry-After.

troubleshoots.symptom: brief, stale, or velocity return empty results
troubleshoots.fix: These read the local mirror: run clarify-pp-cli sync --resources resources --path-context object=deal (and again for person, company, meeting, task) first.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI whenever a task touches Clarify CRM data from a terminal or agent: querying or updating people, companies, deals, meetings, and tasks; bulk imports; pulling meeting transcripts; or answering pipeline questions (stale deals, velocity, follow-up gaps) that Clarify's own API cannot express. It is the offline-capable alternative to Clarify's hosted MCP server.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to send email or run outreach sequences; Clarify is the CRM of record, not a sending tool.
Do not use it for other CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot, Close) — it only speaks to api.clarify.ai.
Do not use it to transcribe new meetings; it retrieves transcripts Clarify has already produced.
Do not use dynamic-list SQL commands to run arbitrary analytics upstream; use the local search and analytics commands against the mirror instead.

recipes.explanation: Attendees, their company, open deals, and past-transcript excerpts in one compact payload.

recipes.title: Find the week's dropped balls
recipes.explanation: Meetings with no follow-up activity, comment, or task on the linked deal or company.

recipes.title: Narrow a big deal query for an agent
recipes.command: clarify-pp-cli objects resources get my-workspace deal --agent --select data.attributes.name,data.attributes.amount,data.attributes.stage
recipes.explanation: JSON:API responses are deep; --select with dotted paths keeps only the fields the agent needs.

recipes.title: Upsert a lead by email
recipes.command: clarify-pp-cli objects records create my-workspace person --match-on email_addresses --data-type person --data-attributes '{"name":{"first_name":"Jane","last_name":"Doe"},"email_addresses":{"items":["jane@example.com"]}}' --dry-run
recipes.explanation: match_on turns the insert into an upsert against the person unique field; drop --dry-run to send it.
